Graduate Research School Scholarships (UQGRSS) – includes Research Training Program (RTP)

Enrolment status
Future UQ student, Current UQ student
Student type
Domestic, International
Study level
Postgraduate research (HDR)
Study area
All study areas
Scholarship focus
Academic excellence
Funding type
Living stipend, Tuition fees
Scholarship value
Living stipend of $39,220 per annum tax free (2026 rate), indexed annually, Single Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC)
Scholarship duration
3.5 years with the possibility of 1 extension in line with UQ and RTP Scholarship Policy
Number awarded
May vary

About this scholarship

These scholarships include a living stipend to support you as you complete a research project for your Doctor of Philosophy, Master of Philosophy or a research-focused professional doctorate at UQ.

Eligibility

You're eligible if you're:

  • nominated by an enrolling school or institute at UQ
  • assessed by the Graduate Research School as meeting all conditions for admission to the higher degree by research program.

How to apply

Before you apply

  1. Check your eligibility for a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) or Master of Philosophy.
  2. Identify a advisor in your field with expertise that's relevant to your proposed project. How to choose an advisor
  3. Prepare your documentation.

When you apply

To apply for this scholarship, submit an expression of interest (EOI) for your preferred program. You don't need to apply separately for this scholarship. How to submit an EOI

In your EOI, complete the 'Scholarship/Sponsorship' section with the following details:

  1. Are you applying for an advertised project: 'No'
  2. Are you applying for (or have you been awarded) a non-UQ scholarship or sponsorship: 'No'
  3. Domestic students only – select whether you would like to be considered for a living stipend scholarship in addition to a tuition fee scholarship.

While EOIs are accepted year-round, applications will only be considered for scholarship assessment within the scholarship round dates outlined below.

Steps to Apply

Applying for a Higher Degree by Research program is a 2-step process:

Step 1: Submit an Expression of Interest (EOI)

Your first step is to submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) for your preferred program. The EOI allows us to assess your research background and identify whether a suitable advisor is available and willing to support your project.

We recommend submitting your EOI as early as possible. View the application dates (see below). 

As part of your EOI, you'll need to provide:

  • the name of your proposed advisor
  • details of any scholarship you are applying for or have been awarded
  • previous qualifications
  • referee details
  • English language proficiency information

You'll also need to upload:

  • academic curriculum vitae (CV)/résumé
  • academic transcripts and degree certificates

Before submitting your EOI, ensure your documents meet UQ's requirements.

How to prepare required documents.

Submit an EOI

What happens after you submit an EOI?

Your nominated advisor will review your EOI. You should usually receive a response within 2 weeks but during peak periods such as examination marking, it can take longer.

If your proposed advisor is interested in working with you, they  are likely to contact you to arrange an informal discussion about your research interests and project.

Step 2: Submit a full application

Once your nominated advisor supports your EOI, you will be invited to submit a full application for admission and scholarship consideration.

The full application includes additional information and documents that were not required at the EOI stage.

In some cases, an agent may be required. We recommend identifying agents in advance so you can reach out to them quickly once your EOI is supported.  You do not need to engage an agent at the EOI stage.

Applications from currently enrolled HDR candidates

As a currently enrolled HDR candidate (i.e., in the PhD, MPhil, or DVClinSc programs) you are welcome to apply via the round dates below.  

To apply please complete our online application form.  

You will be asked to supply the following:

  • Details of your candidature
  • Details of your Principal Advisor
  • Current CV
  • Two referees (yes you can use your current advisory team).

Once submitted your Principal Advisor will be sent a form to support your application and your referees will be asked to complete a referee report.

Outcomes will be issued via your student email following the dates listed below.

Application dates

You can submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) at any time during the year.

However, to be considered for a Graduate Research School Scholarship, you must submit your application by the closing date of an advertised scholarship round.

Applications will be assessed according to the published scholarship round schedule, and outcomes will be released on the dates specified for that round (see below).

*Important information: application closing date

By the application closing date, your application must be:

  • fully submitted, including both the Expression of Interest (EOI) and Full Application. Refer here for how to apply. 
  • complete with all required supporting documentation
  • supported by your Principal Advisor (PA)
  • endorsed by the relevant enrolling unit (School or Institute).

Applications that are incomplete or awaiting documentation, support, endorsement, or approval at the closing date will be moved to the next available scholarship round for consideration.

**Eligible commencement intake

Successful applicants will be offered a commencement date in a research quarter that aligns with their current location. For applicants residing outside Australia, a later commencement date may be offered to allow adequate time for visa processing and approval.
 

Your approved commencement quarter will be confirmed as part of the admission and scholarship process. If your visa is approved earlier, please reach out and we can discuss options.

Important information for scholarship applicants

To allow sufficient time for review and approvals, we strongly recommend submitting your full application at least two weeks before the scholarship closing date.

This helps ensure all required advisor and enrolling unit approvals can be completed before the scholarship deadline. Applications that have not received the necessary support and endorsements by the closing date may not be eligible for consideration in that scholarship round.

If you have pending documentation, such as Honours or Master's results, you can still apply. Upload a current transcript when you submit your EOI. You'll need to provide a complete transcript as soon as possible.

Selection criteria

We'll consider your application against the key areas in the scholarship selection rubric (PDF, 113.46 KB), which include:

  • your academic performance, evidence of research capability, quality of research project
  • the quality of your proposed research environment including resourcing
  • the quality of your proposed advisory team including record of successful supervision, appropriate advisory load, complementary expertise.

What happens next

We’ll email you to let you know the outcome of your application. If you're offered a scholarship, you’ll need to accept by the due date.

If you’re a current UQ student, you won’t receive an email until after the final results from your program have been published.

Rules

Domestic students may be eligible to hold a living stipend scholarship on a part-time basis, subject to approval by the Dean of the Graduate Research School.

UQ reserves the right to postpone or cancel scholarship rounds.
